I think that this app is almost perfect for the needs that I have from a to-do app. I believe that two things are missing.

1. I believe that the app would benefit from natural language support. The ability to quickly add a task while imputing a reminder just through text without having to click on other windows saves a lot of time as well as make the workflow smoother. 

2. I have not seen collaboration support. In a lot of other apps similar apps this feature is present and offers the ability to use it not only as a personal to-do app but could work for you if you have a small team and everyone is using apple devices. 

If those two features made it to the app I would be glad to give it 5 stars. Overall great experience.

I interact with this app more than any other on my phone. I’m not exaggerating when I say Things changed my life; I’ve tried paper notes and lists, other competing apps, etc., and Things enables me to manage a workload that once would’ve overwhelmed me. Best in class.

There is no denying that this is undeniably the best task manager that anyone could purchase. It is unequivocally worth every penny. You can use it as simply, or complexly, as you choose, and even within its complexity, the UI is seamlessly simple. I only have one draw back, and truly, it is a minuscule critique. I would find a way for deeper calendar integration, allowing the user to create calendar events, through Things, that are reflected in the native calendar app. That being said, I simply create large-block calendar events, regarding the main idea, and then I flesh out all of my ideas, tasks, and notes within Things.

Too many task apps focus on dates and git ‘er done; but you also want to less urgent things and arrange their components in some logical way. LOVE Things 3. 

Switched from another, very powerful app. 

First reason is that Things is so attractive. Design matters – You’re more likely to use and get value from apps that are nice to look at (and easy to use). 

Second reason is that it’s really easy to use. Easy to do what you want, and find what you need. 

Part of that usefulness is that it’s constrained. My precious task manager could do more things… so intended to go to deep, and creates an overwhelming monster.

I’ve been using this app daily for 4 years. Simple and clean design, not too cluttered, great organization and features.  Great sync to mac app. It’s one of the few apps that I rely on for work and personal use and it’s always been reliable and a pleasure to use. Highly recommended!
Just enough project management without getting too complicated.

Things is elegantly-designed. Though it IS a bit opinionated in how one should manager their tasks (Today, Upcoming), it does provide a structure for folks who need it. The ability to chunk down your multitude of tasks into what you can just do today is very helpful. I prefer flat lists, and I wish that they had the ability to negate the filters (Today, Upcoming, Anytime), but I’ll take it. DO use the free trial on the Mac app to make sure it’s for you, as thankfully all three platforms (iOS, iPadOS, and macOS) work identical, and THAT I can really appreciate. Cultured Code’s attention to detail is second to none. I only wish that the Watch app allowed me to select which filter I want to see, or perhaps only a tag instead of just Today. Minor gripe. If you want or need something a bit more powerful than Apple’s otherwise excellent Reminders, Things may is for you.
